newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends sharply lower, BOK cushions fall.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends sharply lower, BOK cushions fall.

text.p: The won fell sharply on Wednesday, establishing a new six-year closing low, pounded by the trade deficit, dollar short covering and import deals, traders said.
Dealers said the won could have declined even further if not for mid-afternoon dollar selling support from the central bank.
The won closed at 839.40, down from an opening of 837.00. It fluctuated widely between 836.60 and 843.00.
The closing rate was the lowest level since South Korea started interbank won/dollar trading in 1990, dealers said.
"If not for the central bank intervention, the dollar could have risen over 850," a foreign bank dealer said.
"The central bank's intention seems to be to slow the dollar's rise, not stop it," he said.
The previous record low was set on Tuesday, when the won/dollar rate closed at 836.30.
Traders said the won was likely to continue to be weak because the market was still short in dollars and more large scale importer settlements were due.

"We think we've seen the top for this month, however," said a European bank dealer. He forecast cautious range trading Thursday around 837-841. The Bank of Korea set Thursday's base mid-rate at 839.30, compared to Wednesday's 835.
